turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `composition` (absorber), `architecture` (n-i-p =
regular, p-i-n = inverted), `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode),
`etl` (electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Each row is a device
CONFIGURATION whose efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently
fabricated cells, so it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single
champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_open_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_open_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
I'll systematically analyze the training data to identify the key device physics principles driving high PCE, then apply them to the candidate pool.

## Step 1: Extract Patterns from Training Data

### Composition trends (top performers >20%):
- **FAMAPbBrI** dominates the highest PCEs (19–22.9%)
- **CsFAMAPbBrI** also very strong (17–20.6%)
- **FAMAPbI** competitive (14–20.4%)
- **FAPbI** reaches ~20.2%
- Mixed Pb halide perovskites with FA+MA cations consistently outperform single-cation systems

### Architecture:
- Both nip and pin achieve top PCEs; nip slightly more represented at very top
- nip with SnO2 or TiO2/mp + Spiro-MeOTAD + Au is the dominant high-PCE motif

### ETL patterns for high PCE:
- **SnO2-np** (nip): very strong — multiple entries 17–22%
- **TiO2-c | TiO2-mp** (nip): classic high performer, especially with interface modifiers
- **SnO2-c** (nip): strong (15–18%)
- **C60 | BCP** (pin): good for pin architecture
- **PCBM-60 | C60 | BCP** (pin): strong for pin

### HTL patterns:
- **Spiro-MeOTAD** (nip): by far the most common high-PCE HTL
- **PTAA** (pin): strong for pin
- **NiO-c** (pin): good
- **2PACz** (pin): emerging high performer

### Back contact:
- **Au** (nip): highest PCE entries
- **Ag** (pin): standard
- **Cu** (pin): excellent with PTAA

### Deposition:
- **Spin-coating** or **Spin-coating >> Spin-coating** (two-step): consistently high
- Two-step processes often improve film quality

### Substrate:
- **SLG | FTO** (nip): dominant for highest PCE
- **SLG | ITO** (pin): standard

---

## Step 2: Identify Key Device Physics Principles

**Band alignment**: SnO2 (CBM ~4.0 eV) aligns well with FAMAPbBrI/FAPbI (~3.9 eV), minimizing interface recombination. TiO2-mp provides large contact area. Spiro-MeOTAD HOMO (~5.1 eV) aligns with perovskite VBM (~5.4 eV for I-rich).

**Interface recombination**: Bilayer ETLs (TiO2-c | TiO2-mp, SnO2-c | SnO2-np) reduce pinholes and provide better coverage. Interface modifiers (PCBA, C9, ImAcHcl, CsPbCl3-QDs) passivate traps.

**Film quality**: Two-step spin-coating for FAMAPbBrI/FAMAPbI gives better crystallinity. Anti-solvent methods implicit in spin-coating protocols.

**Contact selectivity**: Au back contact with Spiro-MeOTAD gives ohmic contact for nip. Cu with PTAA gives excellent selectivity in pin.

---

## Step 3: Score Each Candidate

I'll focus on candidates most resembling the top training configurations:

**Top training benchmarks to match:**
1. FAMAPbBrI | OAPbI, nip, SLG|FTO, TiO2-c|TiO2-mp, OAI|DM, Au → 22.91%
2. FAMAPbBrI, nip, SLG|ITO, SnO2-np, CH3O-PEIA|Spiro-MeOTAD, Au → 22.045%
3. FAMAPbBrI, nip, SLG|FTO, TiO2-c|TiO2-mp|Trimethylamine oxide, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au → 21.3%
4. FAMAPbBrI, nip, SLG|FTO, TiO2-c|TiO2-mp, SrCl2|Spiro-MeOTAD, Au → 20.81%
5. CsFAMAPbBrI, pin, SLG|FTO, SnO2-c, Alkoxy-PTEG, Au → 20.6%

**Candidate analysis:**

**c047** — FAMAPbBrI, nip, SLG|ITO, SnO2-c, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au, Spin-coating
- FAMAPbBrI + nip + SnO2-c + Spiro-MeOTAD + Au: matches training entries at 16.45–18.5%. SnO2-c is excellent ETL. Very close to c008 analog. Expected ~17–19%.

**c008** — FAMAPbI, nip, SLG|ITO, SnO2-c, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au, Spin-coating >> Spin-coating
- FAMAPbI + nip + SnO2-c + Spiro-MeOTAD + Au + two-step: matches training "FAMAPbI, nip, SLG|ITO, SnO2-c, Spiro-MeOTAD, Ag, Spin-coating|Dropcasting → 18.5%" and "FAMAPbI, nip, SLG|FTO, SnO2-c, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au → 17.02%". Two-step deposition on ITO with Au contact. Expected ~18–19%.

**c085** — CsFAMAPbBrI, pin, SLG|ITO, C60|BCP, PTAA|PFN-Br, Cu, Spin-coating
- CsFAMAPbBrI + pin + C60|BCP + PTAA|PFN-Br + Cu: Very similar to "CsFAMAPbBrI, pin, SLG|ITO, C60|BCP, 2PACz, Cu → 18.925%" and "CsFAMAPbBrI, pin, SLG|FTO, C60|BCP, PTAA, Cu → 20.1%". PTAA|PFN-Br is a well-known high-performance HTL stack. Cu back contact with PTAA is excellent. Expected ~19–21%.

**c079** — FAMAPbBrI, nip, SLG|FTO, SnO2-np, CsPbBr3-np|Spiro-MeOTAD, Au, Spin-coating
- FAMAPbBrI + nip + SnO2-np + CsPbBr3-np interface layer + Spiro-MeOTAD + Au: SnO2-np is the best ETL for this composition. CsPbBr3-np as HTL interface modifier is novel but analogous to QD passivation layers seen in training (CuInS2-QDs → 17.3%, CdZnSe@ZnSe-QDs → 8.31%). The SnO2-np + Spiro-MeOTAD + Au combination for FAMAPbBrI reaches 19.5–22% in training. CsPbBr3-np at the HTL interface can passivate grain boundaries. Expected ~19–21%.

**c061** — CsFAPbI, nip, SLG|FTO, SnO2-c|C60-SAM, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au, Spin-coating
- CsFAPbI + nip + SnO2-c|C60-SAM + Spiro-MeOTAD + Au: C60-SAM as ETL interface modifier is excellent for passivation and band alignment. Training shows CsFAPbI nip reaching 17.575% (ZnO-c + Spiro + Au) and 13.4% (TiO2-c + Spiro + Au). SnO2-c is superior to TiO2-c for CsFAPbI. C60-SAM passivation is a known high-performance strategy. Expected ~18–20%.

**c036** — CsFAMAPbBrI, nip, SLG|FTO, NDI;SnO2-np, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au, Spin-coating
- CsFAMAPbBrI + nip + NDI;SnO2-np (NDI as ETL modifier with SnO2-np) + Spiro-MeOTAD + Au: NDI is an n-type organic semiconductor that can improve electron extraction. SnO2-np base is excellent. Training shows CsFAMAPbBrI nip with SnO2-np reaching 17.795–18.01%. NDI modification could push higher. Expected ~18–20%.

**c093** — CsFAMAPbBrI, pin, SLG|FTO, PCBM-60|BCP, PTAA, Ag, Spin-coating
- CsFAMAPbBrI + pin + PCBM-60|BCP + PTAA + Ag: Training shows "CsFAMAPbBrI, pin, SLG|ITO, PCBM-60|BCP, NiO-c|PTAA, Ag → 16.95%" and "CsFAMAPbBrI, pin, SLG|FTO, C60|BCP, PTAA, Cu → 20.1%". FTO substrate for pin is less common but used. PTAA is excellent HTL. PCBM-60|BCP is good ETL. Ag vs Cu slightly lower. Expected ~17–19%.

**c089** — FAMAPbBrI, pin, SLG|ITO, C60, PTAA, Ag, Spin-coating
- FAMAPbBrI + pin + C60 + PTAA + Ag: Training "FAPbI, pin, SLG|ITO, C60, PTAA, Ag → 10.76%" but that's FAPbI. For FAMAPbBrI pin: "FAMAPbBrI, pin, SLG|DWCNTs, C60|BCP, PTAA|PFN-P2, Cu → 15.6%". C60 alone without BCP is less optimal. Expected ~15–17%.

**c059** — CsFAMAPbBrI, nip, SLG|FTO, SnO2-QDs, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au, Spin-coating
- CsFAMAPbBrI + nip + SnO2-QDs + Spiro-MeOTAD + Au: SnO2-QDs is a novel form of SnO2 ETL. Training shows SnO2-np for CsFAMAPbBrI reaching 17.795–18.01%. QD form may have better coverage. Expected ~17–19%.

**c015** — CsFAMAPbBrI|(EPA)PbI, nip, SLG|FTO, TiO2-c|TiO2-mp, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au, Spin-coating
- Bilayer perovskite with EPA passivation + classic TiO2-mp + Spiro + Au: Training "CsFAMAPbBrI|(oFPEA)PbI, nip, SLG|ITO, SnO2-np, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au → 19.695%". EPA is similar to oFPEA (aryl ammonium passivation). TiO2-mp is slightly lower than SnO2-np but still strong. Expected ~17–20%.

**c092** — FAMAPbI, nip, SLG|ITO, SnO2-np, Spiro-MeOTAD, MoO3|Ag, Spin-coating >> Spin-coating
- FAMAPbI + nip + SnO2-np + Spiro-MeOTAD + MoO3|Ag: Training "FAMAPbBrI, nip, SLG|ITO, SnO2-np, Spiro-MeOTAD, Ag → 19.5%" and "CsFAMAPbBrI, nip, SLG|ITO, TiO2-np, Spiro-MeOTAD, MoO3|Ag → 19.6%". FAMAPbI with SnO2-np + two-step + MoO3|Ag is strong. Expected ~18–20%.

**c062** — FAMAPbBrI, nip, SLG|ITO, SnO2-np|PCBM-60, Spiro-MeOTAD, MoO3|Au, Spin-coating >> Spin-coating
- FAMAPbBrI + nip + SnO2-np|PCBM-60 (bilayer ETL) + Spiro-MeOTAD + MoO3|Au + two-step: SnO2-np|PCBM-60 is an excellent bilayer ETL (PCBM-60 passivates SnO2 surface). Training "FAMAPbBrI, nip, SLG|FTO, SnO2-c|BMIMBF4, Spiro-MeOTAD, Ag → 16.92%" and "FAMAPbBrI, nip, SLG|ITO, SnO2-np, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au → 19.13–19.5%". Adding PCBM-60 interlayer + MoO3 hole-blocking at back could push higher. Expected ~19–21%.

**c099** — FAMAPbBrI, nip, SLG|FTO, TiO2-c|TiO2-mp, Au-nw|Spiro-MeOTAD, Au, Spin-coating
- FAMAPbBrI + nip + TiO2-c|TiO2-mp + Au-nw|Spiro-MeOTAD + Au: Au nanowires in HTL can improve conductivity and light trapping. Training "FAMAPbBrI, nip, SLG|FTO, Au-np;SnO2-np, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au → 16.98%" (Au-np in ETL). Au-nw in HTL is different but analogous plasmonic enhancement. TiO2-mp base is strong. Expected ~18–20%.

**c029** — FAMAPbBrI, nip, SLG|FTO, TiO2-c|PCBA, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au, Spin-coating
- FAMAPbBrI + nip + TiO2-c|PCBA + Spiro-MeOTAD + Au: PCBA (phenyl-C61-butyric acid) as ETL modifier on TiO2 is excellent for passivation. Training "FAMAPbBrI, nip, SLG|FTO, SnO2-c|PCBM-60, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au → 14.2%". PCBA on TiO2-c (not mp) may be less optimal than SnO2-based. Expected ~16–18%.

**c034** — CsFAMAPbI, nip, SLG|ITO, TiO2-c|TiO2-mp, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au, Spin-coating >> Spin-coating
- CsFAMAPbI + nip + TiO2-c|TiO2-mp + Spiro-MeOTAD + Au + two-step: Training "CsFAMAPbI, nip, SLG|FTO, TiO2-c|TiO2-mp, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au → 18.66%". ITO substrate instead of FTO, two-step deposition. Expected ~18–19%.

**c091** — FAMAPbBrI, nip, SLG|FTO, TiO2-c|TiO2-mp, Spiro-MeOTAD|NaYF4, Au, Spin-coating
- FAMAPbBrI + nip + TiO2-c|TiO2-mp + Spiro-MeOTAD|NaYF4 + Au: NaYF4 upconversion nanoparticles in HTL. Training "FAMAPbBrI, nip, SLG|FTO, TiO2-c|TiO2-mp, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au → 18.98%". NaYF4 can enhance light harvesting via upconversion. Expected ~18–20%.

**c019** — FAMAPbBrI, nip, SLG|FTO, TiO2-c|TiO2-mp, DM, Au, Spin-coating
- FAMAPbBrI + nip + TiO2-c|TiO2-mp + DM (dopant-free HTL) + Au: Training "FAMAPbBrI|OAPbI, nip, SLG|FTO, TiO2-c|TiO2-mp, OAI|DM, Au → 22.91%". DM alone (without OAI passivation) is the HTL from the top-performing device. Expected ~19–21%.

**c057** — FAMAPbBrI, nip, SLG|FTO, TiO2-c|TiO2-mp, X25, Au, Spin-coating
- FAMAPbBrI + nip + TiO2-c|TiO2-mp + X25 (novel HTL) + Au: Similar to other novel HTL entries in training (SFXDAnCBZ → 17.65%, FDT → 17.0%, A101 → 11.42%). X25 is likely a carbazole/spiro-type HTL. Expected ~16–18%.

**c049** — CsFAMAPbBrI, nip, SLG|FTO, TiO2-c|TiO2-mp, Carbozole@S12, Au, Spin-coating
- Training "CsFAMAPbBrI, nip, SLG|FTO, TiO2-c|TiO2-mp, Carbozole@S14, Au → 13.27%". S12 vs S14 variant — similar performance expected. Expected ~13–14%.

---

## Step 4: Final Ranking

Based on device physics analysis:

**c085** (CsFAMAPbBrI, pin, C60|BCP, PTAA|PFN-Br, Cu): The combination of CsFAMAPbBrI with C60|BCP ETL, PTAA|PFN-Br HTL stack, and Cu back contact is the closest analog to the 20.1% training entry (C60|BCP, PTAA, Cu). PFN-Br interlayer improves PTAA wettability and band alignment, likely pushing above 20%.

**c019** (FAMAPbBrI, nip, TiO2-c|TiO2-mp, DM, Au): DM is the exact HTL from the 22.91% champion device (FAMAPbBrI|OAPbI with OAI|DM). Without the OAI passivation layer, performance will be lower but DM alone on standard FAMAPbBrI with TiO2-mp is expected to be very high (~20–21%).

**c062** (FAMAPbBrI, nip, SnO2-np|PCBM-60, Spiro-MeOTAD, MoO3|Au): SnO2-np is the best ETL for FAMAPbBrI. PCBM-60 interlayer passivates SnO2 surface defects. Two-step deposition improves film quality. MoO3 improves Au contact. Expected ~19–21%.

**c079** (FAMAPbBrI, nip, SnO2-np, CsPbBr3-np|Spiro-MeOTAD, Au): SnO2-np ETL + CsPbBr3-np as HTL interface passivation layer. CsPbBr3-np can passivate grain boundaries at the perovskite/HTL interface. Training shows SnO2-np + Spiro + Au for FAMAPbBrI reaching 19.13–22%. Expected ~19–21%.

**c015** (CsFAMAPbBrI|(EPA)PbI, nip, TiO2-c|TiO2-mp, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au): Bilayer perovskite with EPA (aryl ammonium) passivation. Training analog (oFPEA)PbI passivation with SnO2-np reached 19.695%. TiO2-mp is slightly weaker ETL but the EPA passivation is strong. Expected ~18–20%.

**Final: c085, c019, c062, c079, c015**
